entities.summary:
Cleitus the Black (b. 374 BCE, Macedonia) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Macedonia. He is known for his military leadership and was a key figure in the succession of Alexander the Great.

Cleitus the Black played a crucial role in the establishment of the Antigonid dynasty, which ruled Macedon after Alexander's death. His leadership was instrumental in maintaining order and stability in the region, which was crucial for the continuation of trade and cultural exchange between Greece and Asia Minor.

The legacy of Cleitus the Black can be seen in the enduring influence of the Antigonid dynasty on the development of Hellenistic kingdoms and the subsequent Roman Empire. His military campaigns and administrative reforms also had a lasting impact on the organization and tactics of the ancient Macedonian army.

Cleitus the Black's remarkable life and achievements have been immortalized in the accounts of ancient historians such as Plutarch and Arrian, who described him as a shrewd and ambitious leader who was not afraid to challenge the authority of his successors.

In the world of classical scholarship, Cleitus the Black remains a fascinating figure, whose life and reign offer valuable insights into the complexities of ancient Macedonian politics and society.
